what_its_for: Fluvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol and fats (triglycerides) in your blood. It helps reduce your risk of heart attack, stroke, and other heart problems by slowing down the production of cholesterol in your liver.
how_to_take: Take fluvastatin by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the extended-release tablet (Lescol XL) whole — do not crush, chew, or break it. The regular capsule (Lescol) is usually taken in the evening or at bedtime. Take it the same time each day to help you remember. Keep taking this medicine even if you feel well, as high cholesterol usually has no symptoms.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your cholesterol levels and other medications. The usual starting dose is 20 to 40 mg once a day at bedtime (capsule), or 80 mg once a day (extended-release tablet). Your doctor may adjust your dose over time. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store fluvastatin at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of grapefruit juice while taking fluvastatin, as it may increase the amount of medicine in your blood. Limit or avoid alcohol, which can raise your risk of liver problems. Do not start any new supplements, vitamins, or over-the-counter medicines (especially niacin, antacids, or cholesterol-lowering supplements) without checking with your pharmacist or doctor first, as some can interact with fluvastatin.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, weakness, or cramps (especially with fever or dark-colored urine, which could be signs of a serious muscle problem called rhabdomyolysis); yellowing of your skin or eyes; severe stomach pain; unusual tiredness; or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Fluvastatin starts working in your body right away, but it may take 4 to 6 weeks before you see a significant change in your cholesterol levels. Your doctor will check your cholesterol with a blood test after about 4 to 8 weeks. Most people need to take this medicine long-term, along with a healthy diet and exercise, to keep their cholesterol under control.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use fluvastatin if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It can harm an unborn baby or nursing infant. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine and tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Children: Fluvastatin may be prescribed for children aged 9 and older with inherited high cholesterol, but only under a doctor's supervision. Older adults (65+): This medicine can generally be used safely in older adults, but your doctor may monitor you more closely for muscle or liver problems. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have any liver or kidney problems before starting this medicine, as your dose may need to be adjusted or this medicine may not be right for you.
